mentions.name: Linux printing & scanning stack improvements
mentions.description: This project improves the Linux printing and scanning stack—CUPS, SANE, AirSane, legacy drivers, and x86 proprietary driver emulation on ARM via Box86—fixing basic bugs and low-hanging-fruit optimizations in a 20+ year old stack maintained by only a handful of people, ahead of the CUPS v3 shift to modern driverless printing.
mentions.problem: The Linux printing stack is 20+ years old, still full of basic bugs and easy optimizations, maintains legacy compatibility with roughly 5 driver architectures and 4 user-selectable rasterizers, and is supported by only four people (scanning by a single person).
mentions.source_excerpt: Spent about 2 years improving printing and scanning stack of Linux: CUPS, SANE, AirSane, as well as some legacy drivers, and also x86 proprietary driver emulation on ARM with Box86.
